summary: Feed s142_double is degraded: 51.1% of TCP sessions are one-way (67/131) and 11.6% of packets are duplicates (206/1775), preventing NDR from reconstructing full sessions.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction of many TCP flows to this NDR tool port. Most likely asymmetric routing with ingress from two different TAP/SPAN points not aggregated, or per-packet load-balancing splitting directions across different tools. NDR requires both directions (profile needs_both_directions=true).
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reassemble TCP streams, misses handshakes and stateful detection, generates false one-way flow alerts and loses ~51% session visibility for threat detection.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each 5-tuple to the same NDR tool port so bidirectional sessions are restored for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: 11.6% duplicate packets indicates same packet arriving via two paths - typically SPAN/mirror duplication or TAP aggregation from both sides of a link without deduplication enabled on the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate processing, inflates flow/packet counts, skews analytics and can cause false positives or missed detections due to sequence confusion.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication within a short window to strip identical packets before delivery while preserving one correct copy for the NDR.
